#3753. Sony squeezes out a PlayStation 5 firmware update before the release of GTA 6

Sony has managed to squeeze out another PlayStation 5 firmware update before the highly-anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto 6.

Sony has been rolling firmware updates out on a fairly regular basis, and like many of those updates, this latest one - version 26.07-14.23.00 - doesn't bring any very meaningful changes. Sony repeated the same "we've made some security fixes to the system software" patch-note that we've seen many times before.

And like all those firmware updates, 26.07-14.23.00 is mandatory for all PS5 and PS5 Pro consoles, assuming you want to go online or play the latest games. That, of course, includes GTA 6, which requires the console's firmware to be updated to its latest version before you can play.

The update should download automatically the next time you turn on your console, but you can also force the download through Settings > System > System Software > System Software Update and Settings. This is also where you can tick the option for your console to automatically download and install those updates in the future.

Although Sony hasn't directly said so, the high frequency of those security firmware updates is likely related to the impending release of GTA 6, especially in light of recent gen-AI-driven PS5 jailbreaks.

Any firmware released before GTA 6's release now becomes required to play the game, which delays potential security exploits, seeing as hackers would need to find vulnerabilities in that firmware in order to play. While this may never happen, Sony is at least trying to minimise the risk as much as possible.

GTA 6 arrives 19th November on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It is now available to pre-load for anyone who pre-ordered the digital version, and those with the code-in-box physical version.

The hype surrounding the long-awaited release of Grand Theft Auto VI has reached a fevered pitch, with reviews for the game universally saying it’s living up to that hype. The GTA series has consistently been one of the most popular gaming franchises of all time, and one of the most successful entertainment franchises on Earth. It’s also one of the only monster franchises that hasn’t been adapted as a movie or a TV show.

That’s always surprised me, because it seems ripe for a video game adaptation, right? Now, the CEO of Take-Two Interactive, the company that owns Rockstar, the studio that produces the games, was recently asked about a possible adaptation. His answer is actually kind of positive news, though hardly concrete evidence that an adaptation is on the way.

While appearing on The David Rubenstein Show, CEO Strauss Zelnick was asked about the possibility of a movie. He responded:

We're very careful about line extensions because this is a creative company, and our goal is to make the best entertainment on Earth.  Entertainment we’re always proud of. We would make a movie or a television show based on our intellectual property if our creative teams were passionate about it, if they thought that would somehow engage and delight our consumers. It's a high bar to do that, and, of course, there's always a risk of failure. So we don't rule it out, but we're very, very selective.

“Line extensions” are when business use existing products or intellectual property to expand how they can take advantage of markets, like, for example, video game movie adaptations. Take-Two, as Zelnick points out, has been very careful with how they’ve expanded their brands outside of video games. No franchise shows that more than GTA. It seems ripe for adaptation and really has been for decades, but they have yet to pull the trigger. They do seem open to it, though.

Like millions of other people, I’m still waiting for a few more hours to be able to play GTA VI, as we all have been for years now. Based on the glowing reviews, this could be the version of the game most likely to get adapted into a movie. Reviews have talked about the storyline in the new game, praising it for how well the story is incorporated into the game. It seems full of drama (and great music). Plus, there are two playable protagonists, a couple named Jason and Lucia.

This is the first time GTA has featured a female playable character, and it tells the story of the two, which to me sounds like the perfect basis for a possible film. While the characters in previous versions have been fun, these two actually sound like the most realistic characters, with a deep backstory together. That really leaves the option open.

It’s also worth mentioning that Zelnick, who took over Take-Two in 2007, has a history in the movie world as the former President of 20th Century Fox and overseeing hit movies like Home Alone and before that worked for Columbia Pictures Television. If anyone knows how to strike a good deal for Take-Two, it’s Zelnick. I would love to see it happen one day!

#3751. Space station horror-FPS Derelikt is a lively retro throwback to Alien: Resurrection, though it's better at shooting than scaring

I'm a reasonable man. I don't expect every PS1-styled, cosmic horror, nakedly Alien: Resurrection-homaging retro FPS to suffocate me under a blanket of misery. Some of the lighter moments in Derelikt, which released last week, even land: I was grinning my cheeks off as I gorged on the Eldtrich knowledge sealed within an alien obelisk, while repeatedly hanging up on the aghast scientist who kept videocalling me to stop.

Still, Derelikt is fortunate that it's a good shooter, as it often gets muddled on whether it wants to be a horror game as well. It certainly threatens the spooks, trapping you in an oppressively dingy asteroid rig in the orbit of Saturn - the scariest of the ringed gas giants! - and warping most of the other staff into vaguely echinodemic monsterpeople. Also, opening the inventory reveals it to be made of rectangles, a classic symptom of a video game character about to get mangled in the nerves and face.

But nah, shotgun go boom boom. It turns out Derelikt's derelict dwellers are both perfectly susceptible to mundane lead, and sparing users of ambush tactics at most; several even stand around with their backs turned, as if waiting for you to surprise them with a lethal pipe swing. And, even on Medium difficulty, the opening spell of fight-or-run scarcity quickly gives way to an abundance of ammo and health pickups that can easily fill the pocket grid to bursting. I don't claim to have been playing perfectly, but I'm about halfway through and the only way I see myself running low on bullets is if I start using them to punch the complete works of Thomas Campion into a wall.

It's indecisive tonally, as well. The dialogue, and there are a fair few survivors to chat with, seems interested in emulating the gravitas-starved, "Woah man" style of New Millennium action game scripts. Which I can sort of see the logic behind, given the visuals and sound design also, and arguably much more painstakingly, mimic that era. But the downside remains that it ends up with a gravitas-starved, "Woah man" style, just with an extra dash of sideways-winking awareness. Again, it only sometimes works, and it's never scary or eerie. But then there are also more earnest attempts to spin uneasiness, with pages of deranged scribbles left behind by the dwindling crew, and at least a couple of genre-classic wall daubings, which tend to leave me wishing developers Visuwyg had just picked a lane.

Again, though, underneath all the smartarsing is a quality little shooter. The retro presentation does little to soften the heavy, industrial kick of its gunfire, and although many of the meatier freaks are more absorbent than they look, their pained thrashing really helps sell the impact of every individual shot. I also don't really mind the lack of Dead Spacey surprise attacks, as the station's narrow confines tend to force you into tenser, close-range encounters in an organic way anyhow.

More impressive still is how Derelikt manages to fabricate a cold, apprehensive atmosphere befitting its fallen space base, in direct defiance of its own quasi-comedic script. This is mainly thanks to the clanging, low-lit station itself, which teases you with just enough flashes of comfort – a stretch of marble floor here, a messy rec room there – to make your quick return to its steel guts feel all the more unpleasant. Some credit must also go to the puzzling, the cardkey hunts and code searches of which initially had me fearful of the more obstinate, opaque, classic horror style preferred by fellow backwards-looker Silver Pines. Instead, it's more like a compacted Deus Ex, hinting at the need to peek at people's computers and scour the environments for the needed codes. Which makes for generally smoother progress, yes, but also gets you more involved and present inside Derelikt's infested walls.

Midway-through impressions, then: it's a little silly, and perhaps a little confused, but Derelikt finds its focus whenever something needs making dead. I shall continue blasting xenos and burning my eyes out with magic rocks until – no, madam, please hold – further notice.

#3750. After GTA 6's original soundtrack, Justice probably won't work on any other video game ever again

You've probably heard at least a little bit of the Grand Theft Auto 6 soundtrack from French electronic duo, Justice: a single taken from the act's original soundtrack has been released as a standalone track, and was the accompaniment to GTA 6's launch trailer. Featuring Tame Impala, SZA, and the fantastic King Gizzard and the Lizard Wizard, it's clear that the duo - and Rockstar - have spared no expense on the production of music for the game.

From what we've heard so far, it's all very good: synth-drenched and poppy, a perfect mix of modern electronica and nostalgic throwback - ideal for the Miami-based setting of Vice City. You ought to enjoy the music while you can, though, because it seems Justice won't be coming back to video games any time soon. If ever.

Via a new interview with French publication Rockyrama, Justice's two members - Gaspard Augé and Xavier de Rosnay - shed a little light about their work with Rockstar, and their inspiration for joining the project. "When [the offer to work with Rockstar] arrived on the table, we thought 'if there’s one video game we have to do, it's this one.' As soon as we accepted and started working [on the OST], we thought it would probably be the first and last score we’ll ever do for a video game."

Interesting. The duo, from the clip we can see on Rockyrama's posts, don't seem to give more information about this decision - did they have a bad time working with Rockstar? Was it intense? Or is it rather down to the fact that, if you're going to work on a game, you may as well make it what is largely expected to be the biggest game of all time.

Justice, for what it's worth, consider the work they've done on GTA 6 to be "a real album" of music - it's not seen as lesser or different to the band, just because it's being released as part of a video game. "GTA 6 gave us the excuse and direction to do it. The music always had to be listenable on its own, even if each track is tailored for [a specific] scene," the band explains.

The band's album isn't the only music connected to the game, either. There's also a 34-song album launching for the game, composed of original songs from some of the biggest artists in the world. The album features Travis Scott, Rina Sawayama, Cardi B, Pinkpantheress, SZA, Keith Richards, Dua Lipa, Jennie, Lana Del Rey, Zara Larsson and many more. The full tracklist leaked at the weekend.

GTA 6 is finally here, and it's already smashing records, standing as the highest-rated game of all time with just one day under its belt – but that might not be enough to save developer Rockstar Games from further rounds of layoffs, some believe.

Jacob Novak, former financial lead at Square Enix, is one such person. Taking to X to share his thoughts on potential Rockstar redundancies – a topic that's been circulating following words from animation programmer Nestor Uriarte – he asserts, "There will, of course, be major layoffs at Rockstar." After all, "They've built the biggest, most expensive game of all time and now released it." But why does that matter?

Well, it boils down to the "team size" Rockstar required during production versus what it needs now, post-launch, according to Novak. "Part of the team will move onto GTA 6's online mode, part to DLC, but the team size required to ship this is not the team size required to build continuous content." It's a tough thought to consider, but I suppose it does make a bit of sense – although that's not to say it guarantees layoffs.

Novak believes they're incoming, however. "It's likely that Rockstar has been waiting until after the game ships, not wanting the layoffs to impact the news cycle or distract in reviews." he writes. "My guess is early Q1 next year with a consulting period starting in the UK." He means early 2027 here, which is only a few months off at this point. The executive cites Take-Two Interactive's finances in a reply then.

Attached is a screenshot of a Google search reading, "What was the last profitable quarter for Take-Two [Interactive]?" Its results state that Take-Two's last profitable quarter was back in 2022. Alongside the image, Novak says "Strauss Zelnick's mission is not going to be to let the profits be absorbed by keeping employees. It is going to be to recoup all his losses." It isn't set in stone, obviously, but it certainly provokes some thought.

It sadly wouldn't be a first for Rockstar, with its "ruthless" 2025 layoffs springing to mind immediately – but it's something I do hope we don't see come to fruition, especially when considering the success that GTA 6 is seeing so far.

Obsession is that one film on the 2026 movie schedule that we can’t stop talking about, and why would we want to? Now we can stream it to our heart's content with a Netflix subscription, I needed to dig up all the fun behind-the-scenes facts I learned from writer/director Curry Barker. Each of these made me think of the movie in a whole different way! Let’s get into it. (SPOILERS ahead.)

I’m always curious about how movies change over time, and Barker told CinemaBlend about one pivotal scene that he played around with a lot. The writer/director was also the movie’s editor on the $750k independent production, and he told us about one exchange he tried a bunch of different ways . In his words:

The scene where they’re driving and she’s talking about romance and love. And she’s saying, like, ‘Hey, you know, you’re the only person I can talk to about this stuff.’ That scene changed so much. There’s probably like ten different versions of that scene. One that’s a little longer, one that’s shorter, one where she doesn’t even say the line, one where she goes into a longer thing. Like, I don’t know why. That scene just has so many different versions of it.

This sort of blew my mind because this is the scene I was playing over and over in my head after seeing the movie. It’s an important scene because it establishes Bear and Nikki’s relationship before Nikki loses her autonomy. Watching that scene made me wonder if Bear could have had a shot with Nikki if he had simply asked her out rather than using the One Wish Willow. With that in mind, I totally see why this scene would have needed tweaking, but I think it's perfect now.

When I first watched Obsession, I felt a chill down my spine when Bear called the number on the back of the One Wish Willow box. Then, I subsequently had so many questions about what was going on! When I talked to Barker about this scene, he revealed he was the one on the other side of the line.

Well, that was me… yeah, that’s my voice. He works for the One Wish Willow Company, he kind of answers their phone calls. He handles all the complaints of all the wishes. But, there’s no, I mean, I like to keep it pretty vague. I think you could think of it as some sort of purgatory that [Nikki’s] being kept in, right?

What a fun cameo! I had no idea Barker was the voice, but it’s a fun little tidbit I’ll always think about when I watch that scene. He gave us some interesting insight about what’s going on with that phone call, too. I'm never forgetting Nikki's screams on the other line.

One more BTS detail I want to share has to do with what didn’t make it into the film. Obsession really goes hard in the paint on the movie rating scale, so I was curious if there was a scene the director had to remove because it went too far. The answer is, yes, there was one moment.

There was only one thing I had to take out because it was too far, but other than that they really let me do whatever they wanted. And, I was kind of, like, shocked. This movie really felt like a bunch of kids getting together and making something, and hoping that the parents don’t come home. They never did. Nobody ever stopped us, and we just kept making the thing we wanted to make. Like, even the way we shot it. We thought someone was going to tell us to turn the lights on.

So, what was that “one thing”? During a Q&A (via Deadline), Barker revealed it was the scene where Nikki kills Sarah by smashing her head into the steering wheel. Barker said there was originally “about six or seven more smashes." The MPA ratings board was going to give the movie a NC-17 rating because of it. At first, Barker wasn’t happy about making the change, but when he saw the movie with an audience (and heard their reactions), he realized the number they landed on was “the right number” to choose.

You can check out the rest of our Obsession interview on CinemaBlend's YouTube. There we also talked about that gross cat scene and what probably happens after the ending. I know I’m always finding new theories online. Obsession really is the movie of the year for this horror fan, and I loved learning these behind-the-scenes facts.

#3747. "Encouraging players to return is no mean feat" - Square Enix tempts Final Fantasy 14 players back with free game-time to fill void before new expansion

"People pause their adventures for all kinds of reasons."

Final Fantasy 14 is between expansions at the moment, with Evercold preparing for release in February. So, in order to keep the game populated for the next few months, Square Enix is running a special promotion in hopes of tempting players back in.

This promotion, which began yesterday, offers players a choice between two enticing freebies. Lapsed players who haven't logged in for over six months are to be given 30 days of free game time to hop back in and catch up with the main story quest ahead of Evercold's release.

In addition, there's an alluring character skip available too. If your FF14 character is at least level 90 on one class - the current level-cap is 100 - you can skip all the way to the final part of the latest Dawntrail expansion. You still need to grind to level 100 in preparation for Evercold, but the aforementioned free month of game time should provide plenty of time to do so.

In a producer letter written to accompany this promotion, Naoki Yoshida provided insight into why this was being implemented, stating that retaining players in an MMO like FF14 was of the "utmost importance".

"Encouraging players to return is no mean feat", Yoshida wrote. "People pause their adventures for all kinds of reasons, including dissatisfaction and loss of interest. Although we continually update the game to address such issues, the fact remains that getting players to resume their journey is a difficult task indeed.

"For one, I feel that the pace of change in our lives is growing increasingly fast. Back when A Realm Reborn launched, I set policies in place based on the idea that significant changes in life usually happened in roughly three-year cycles. With that in mind, we've done our best to avoid heavy-handed attempts to secure player retention through game design, and we still maintain that philosophy even today."

Yoshida went on to explain that promotions such as this are meant as a "tiny nudge". He notes that those who have retained subscriptions continuously remain "the most important" players in the development team's eyes, and acknowledges that the process of catching up in an MMO can seem "daunting" for many.

This problem of player retention is nothing new for MMOs, especially in the tricky time between the end of a current expansion and the beginning of a new one. MMO popularity often waxes and wanes, with a new expansion acting as an exciting call to action, with the months leading up to it often serving as a natural break-point for many. Still, monthly subs pay the bills, so keeping folks around even during these quiet months is important.

Final Fantasy 14: Evercold is looking like an especially exciting expansion. On top of the new story and two classes being added, the game is getting an overhaul to combat, with both classic Reborn and Evolved action modes, as well as a new raid difficulty meant to bridge the gap between normal and savage tiers.

The game has certainly come a long way since its initial release back in 2010. Dawntrail proved divisive among fans too, though with Evercold there's a lot of hope that a new overarching storyline can bring the steal back the hearts of players old and new.

I feel like I say this once a week at this point, but gaming monitors occupy one of the only bright spots in the dark cloud that is PC hardware right now. They are getting better and cheaper by the day, and it seems I'm not alone in thinking this, as global OLED monitor shipments doubled in the last year. Woo, go OLED monitors.

This is according to Trendforce, which notes Asus is the market leader for global OLED monitor sales (at 21.7%), with MSI coming in second (14.5%) and Samsung coming in third (11.3%). LGE take fourth place with 8.6%, and Dell closely follows that with 8.2%. The rest of the industry has the remaining 35.7% to split among themselves.

As for total sales, Trendforce says global OLED sales got a 13% bump from last quarter to this year, and more impressively, sales for OLED monitors reportedly doubled compared to the same quarter last year. That means OLED monitors have significant upward momentum right now.

And who can blame people for buying in? OLED monitors are known for having super vibrant colours, true blacks, and they tend to have wicked fast response times and refresh rates. The difference between IPS and OLED is so apparent when you put them beside each other, and I know, as I'm rocking a dual monitor setup with both panel technologies.

They are a bit more expensive than IPS, and older panels can suffer from burn-in, but I can say swapping from an IPS panel to an OLED one is one of the most monumental changes I've made to my gaming setup in the last decade. Though, in fairness, that also came with a resolution bump from 1080p to 1440p.

OLEDs have been getting cheaper over time, too—they're far from the ultra-expensive pieces of kit we saw just a couple of years ago. And with new manufacturing developments such as inkjet printing (IJP), there's every reason to believe the downward trend in pricing could continue.

What great news to hit just as Black Friday has started at Amazon. If you're feeling the hankering to stare into the vibrant blacks of an OLED panel, there are already some sweet savings to be had. Now that OLED gaming monitors are as cheap as $270, they're a seriously attractive upgrade option.

#3745. Is it time to retire Dragon Quest as a series? Chrono Trigger composer Yasunori Mitsuda thinks it might be

Chrono Trigger composer Yasunori Mitsuda thinks it may be time for Square Enix to retire Dragon Quest, while reflecting on the direction of the popular RPG series after Akira Toriyama's death. The mangaka, whose art and distinct style were foundational to Chrono Trigger and Chrono Cross - and are still used in Dragon Quest to this day - died in 2024 at the age of 68.

Today, speaking via a blog post on his personal website (hat tip, Power Up Gaming), Mitsuda - a colleague of Toriyama's back in the SNES/Chrono Trigger days - suggested that maybe it's time to retire the franchise in favour of something new. This was all triggered by the announcement of Dragon Quest RPG: The Island of the Demon Tree and the Guided Island, an iOS and Android game that uses art that is very reminiscent of Toriyama's.

"The Toriyama-style illustrations for [Dragon Quest RPG] have become a hot topic, but I feel that this direction is not good for the artist, Toriyama Akira fans, and even for the late Toriyama Akira himself," said Mitsuda. "As a personal opinion, since it's impossible to create anything truly new no matter how hard you try, I feel that the Dragon Quest series should be brought to an end for now, and [Dragon Quest creator, Yuji Horii] should create a new RPG. (There have been many remakes already.)"

Horii himself seems undeterred: with the new mobile game's announcement last week, he noted that the goal of his new project is to "capture that unmistakable Dragon Quest feeling" that comes with "exploring towns, meeting new allies, gearing up and steadily growing stronger". As Mitsuda calls for the series to retire, and for something new to take its place, Horii is keen to bring "the same classic adventure" to your smartphone.

"What's important is that the game provides dreams, hope, and experiences that can only be had through games to the younger generation of children who will play it in the future," concluded Mitsuda. "But every time I see topics like this, I realise just how wonderful Dragon Quest is and how it has captivated so many people."

It's unlikely Square Enix is going to want to drop the series, of course: the Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D Remake exceeded Square Enix's (in)famously lofty expectations, and as the company aggressively pursues its multiplatform strategy, it's hard to imagine a world in which it's going to want to move away from a series that routinely pulls in millions of sales.

For your eyes only, here's everything we know about Bond 26

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

It's official: we have a new James Bond. Robert Pattinson will play 007 in Bond 26, directed by Dune filmmaker Denis Villeneuve, for new studio Amazon MGM. Five years after Daniel Craig's last mission, the long wait for Bond to return is almost over.

If the news has left you feeling shaken and stirred, we've got plenty more classified intel below. So read on for everything we know so far about Bond 26, from the people bringing Bond back behind the scenes, to the confirmed cast, to story and release date speculation.

While we wait for 007 to sip a Vesper martini once more, why not check out our recap of how Robert Pattinson became the next James Bond, and our ranking of the best Bond movies.

There is currently no official release date for Bond 26, nor has studio Amazon MGM hinted at a release window. However, given the stage the movie is currently at in production, we can make an educated guess.

Director Denis Villeneuve is about to be a free agent following the release of Dune 3 on December 18, and will presumably be working full-time on Bond 26 from that point, once his Dune 3 promotional duties are complete. The official announcement suggested that screenwriter Steven Knight has completed work on the Bond 26 screenplay, and with Pattinson's casting now confirmed, many of the major pieces are already in place.

Assuming there are no major setbacks, we'd expect a new Bond film to hit screens late 2028 or in 2029. That may seem far away right now, but Bond will be back on screen sooner than you think.

The script for Bond 26 is, of course, a state secret, so exact details about what to expect from Bond 26 are non-existent right now, but the casting of Robert Pattinson is our first big clue.

At 40 years old, Pattinson is older than even Daniel Craig was in Casino Royale, so despite Pattinson still looking fresh-faced, a young Bond story is highly unlikely. Pattinson is something of an unpredictable performer, and an actor who has proven time and time again that he's willing to take risks. However, he can also distill the essence of cool on screen; just check out his performance as Neil in Christopher Nolan's Tenet for evidence of that.

Former Bond writers Neil Purvis and Robert Wade are in agreement on this, telling Deadline that they think Pattinson "has what it takes" to play Bond, adding, "We liked the sly wit he brought to the spy in Tenet, and with this decision it’s clear Denis wants to keep Bond cool.”

What does that mean? Don't expect Pattinson's Bond to be a Craig-style bruiser bulldozing his way through the scenery, nor a Connery-style enforcer. Neither would I expect the cheeky humor of Roger Moore's Bond to creep its way in, given Villeneuve's proclivity for relatively self-serious material. Instead, Timothy Dalton and Pierce Brosnan's eras might be the closest touchstones, at least tonally.

As for what the story could cover, it's likely to have been a fascinating struggle for screenwriter Steven Knight. Bond has always been defined by the era, and much of Ian Fleming's source material has been mined (though often simply for titles rather than plot specifics). What defines a late-2020s Bond? Does traditional, Cold War-era spycraft even have a place in the tech-driven age of AI? And would Amazon go the serialized route of Craig's era that more thoroughly interrogates the Bond persona through past trauma, or opt for the more episodic, self-contained missions of Bonds prior?

Our best guess is that, after Craig, you can't put the toothpaste back in the tube, and Pattinson's Bond will continue to be treated as a character on his own journey, rather than resetting the clock with each outing. And I don't see a world where AI and technology aren't part of Bond's world, but that's all speculation for now.

So far, there is a single confirmed cast member, and that's the man playing James Bond himself, Robert Pattinson. Bond, of course, is the cornerstone the rest of his world needs to be built around, so now that Pattinson is in place, we expect further casting news to come thick and fast.

Assuming Amazon MGM and Denis Villeneuve aren't throwing out the baby with the bathwater and giving us a radically different kind of Bond movie, we'd expect news soon on who will play the villain and the Bond girl in Bond 26. And it's possible we'll also get a new M, Moneypenny, Q, Felix Leiter and more familiar figures.

For now then, the confirmed Bond 26 cast is as follows.

Before Pattinson signed on as the next 007, a number of key creatives were put in place behind the scenes. After Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson sold their controlling stake in Bond to Amazon in February 2025, veteran producers David Heyman (the Harry Potter movies) and Amy Pascal (the Spider-Man movies) were brought on as stewards for the Bond franchise.

It was Heyman and Pascal who hired Dune director Denis Villeneuve to helm Bond 26 in June of the same year. At the time, Heyman and Pascal said, "Denis Villeneuve has been in love with James Bond movies since he was a little boy. It was always his dream to make this movie, and now it's ours, too. We are lucky to be in the hands of this extraordinary filmmaker."

Two months later, in August 2025, it was announced that Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight would pen the screenplay for Bond 26. Prior to Knight, screenwriters Neal Purvis and Robert Wade wrote every Bond movie between 1999's The World is Not Enough and 2021's No Time to Die, including every movie during the Daniel Craig era.

The rest of the Bond 26 team has yet to be officially announced, though there are unconfirmed rumors that Villeneuve and his Dune and Dune: Part Two cinematographer Greig Fraser will re-team for Bond 26, despite Linus Sandgren taking over for Fraser on Dune 3. Sandgren previously served as cinematographer on No Time to Die. For now, we'll have to wait for more news.

There is no trailer for Bond 26 just yet, as the movie hasn't started filming. However, we did get a taste of what's in store with a short casting announcement video that confirmed Robert Pattinson's casting as James Bond. The 26-second-long teaser sees Pattinson's Bond step out of deep shadows wearing a traditional tux, and holding a slightly higher-tech pistol than we're used to from Bond (some have already balked at the idea MI6's finest would use a red dot sight on his weapon of choice).

We also got a first promotional image, shot by photographer Jaap Buitendijk, who says the shadowy effect was achieved using a "tightly focused beam of a Fresnel light". It's unclear if Buitendijk also lit the screentest video, but we do know Villeuve directed it.

It's currently classified information how many missions Pattinson's Bond will embark on, but reporting in the run-up to Pattinson's casting gave us a clear indication about what the future could hold. Per Puck, the terms of Pattinson's deal required the Tenet star to sign on for three movies, which was actually one movie less than other nearly-Bond candidates were required to sign on for. Pattinson is also reportedly being more generously compensated for the role than the other potential Bonds would have been.

So that could mean a trilogy of Pattinson-starring Bond films, if not more (Craig, of course, played Bond in five films across 15 years). We don't yet know if Villeneuve will direct more than one Bond movie either, but he has just helmed a trio of Dune movies, so he's no stranger to shepherding back-to-back productions to the screen.

We'll confirm any further information on Bond 26 right here, as it's disclosed by MI6. In the meantime, check out our guide to all the most exciting upcoming movies heading our way.

One of the best SNL sketches in years is producing some strong reactions.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The goal of sharing a Saturday Night Live sketch is typically to elicit a laugh, but now and again, one makes such a thoughtful or important point that people use it as a conversation starter or as evidence to prove a point. That’s exactly what’s going on with last weekend’s Sister sketch, a fake commercial about how caregiving responsibilities overwhelmingly fall on the women in the family. Tens of thousands have taken to social media to share or retweet the sketch alongside comments about how they feel seen, and now, we’ve reached the point where people are using it to call out their own family members.

Sister has been watched more than five million times in the past few days on YouTube, more than twenty million times on X and untold millions of times more on additional social platforms. If you look at comments on any of these platforms, two immediate themes jump out. Many people are saying they feel exactly like the title sister in the sketch, and many others are calling out family members for not helping with caregiving responsibilities.

Actually, I probably phrased that second one too nicely. What many people are doing is throwing up their middle fingers at family members and telling stories about their avoidance and/ or woeful incompetence. Here’s a story with more than 69,000 likes…

My mom literally called me to come over to help her water a single outdoor plant, and when I got there she was cooking for my older brother who had been there the entire time.

That wild story is definitely not an outlier either. The angry rants are just pouring out of people, an overwhelming majority of whom are women who feel like they are left doing everything while their siblings live their lives. Some are mad about how they did everything until their parent died, only to find out their absentee sibling(s) got the exact same inheritance. Others are mad about how their family members infrequently show up and then critique the job they were doing and question the decisions they make.

One woman shared that a caretaker in her family was later sued by the surviving family members for taking money out of the disabled parent’s bank account to buy said parent food and medicine. You can check out that banger below, which has about five thousand likes…

With Sister you can also wait for her to spend your dad’s money on essentials for him like groceries or clothes and then sue her later - because she never had financial power of attorney!

Seriously, don’t take my word for it. Look wherever the Sister sketch is embedded. You’ll immediately start running into story after story of angry people who need to let it out. I saw one woman calling out the parent they’re looking after for raising her brother to think he didn’t need to help. I’ve seen numerous lawyers, nurses, dementia care workers and doctors saying they see the same dynamic over and over again. I saw one woman say her brother who lives near her mom can’t be bothered to help; so, she has to travel across the country to handle things.

watching this from my mom’s house 1500 miles away bc my brother Just Can’t Manage to get her to the doctor or the dentist. he lives down the street

It’s clear this sketch, which is filled with fun little easter eggs, struck a nerve, but it seems like in a very therapeutic way. It’s allowing people to give voice to frustrations they’ve clearly had for a long time, and if it leads to even some family members doing a little self-reflecting and helping out a bit more, it’ll be a huge victory. You can watch the sketch in full below...

Saturday Night Live is off for a few weeks for the holidays, but it’ll return in early December with the next new episode guest hosted by Amanda Seyfried. Fingers crossed she’s able to give us something that makes even a fraction of the cultural footprint. You can catch previously aired episodes streaming with a Peacock subscription.

#3740. Call of Duty might have swapped guns and tanks for knights and swords if an Infinity Ward experiment had panned out

"If it's a war story, sure, it can be COD."

As much as Call of Duty is criticised for delivering the same thing every year, reports occasionally surface of attempts to take the series in bold new directions, even if none of these experiments have so far seen the light of day. And it turns out a medieval Call of Duty was also explored at one time.

This latest revelation comes from Infinity Ward veteran Taylor Kurosaki, who led development on the studio's Infinite Warfare and 2019 Modern Warfare game. "Call of Duty is a massive tree with a lot of branches, right?" Kurosaki told PC Gamer. "It can be World War 2. The team at IW had prototyped a medieval Call of Duty. Where you were a knight and had a sword and all kinds of crazy shit. But if it's a war story, sure, it can be Call of Duty."

This isn't the first time we've heard of an unusual Call of Duty prototype. When Activision brought Sledgehammer Games into the fold as another lead studio for the lucrative shooter series, the team briefly worked on a third-person horror off-shoot set in Vietnam, which was referred to as Fog of War.

Activision's legal battle with Infinity Ward founders Vince Zampella and Jason West, however, caused the project to be cancelled, as Sledgehammer was roped into helping the studio finish Modern Warfare 3.

As for Kurosaki, he currently leads That's No Moon alongside creative partner Jacob Minkoff and other Infinity Ward and Naughty Dog veterans. The studio is currently working on Crossfire, a narrative-driven third-person shooter set in the universe of Smilegate's free-to-play series of the same name.

My greatest regret about Grand Theft Auto 6's release is that I didn't make an 'angry players' bingo card beforehand. Seriously, with how predictable all the outrage is, I could've had the winning card by now, and the game's not even been out for 24 hours yet.

What would I have on my bingo card? Well, a couple of things that'd be on there are: angry at 30 fps, angry at shooting police (a classic), and slap-bang in the middle I'd have angry that you can't cheat (the other kind of cheat) on your partner.

It seems that there's a group of players who are taking issue with the fact that GTA 6's story revolves around Jason and Lucia's relationship and therefore you can't pick up other women like strippers or Mandy, an early side character who players seem to be quite preoccupied with right now. Although, I haven't heard anyone complain that Lucia can't get with other guys.

You can still go to strip clubs, though. You can even go as a couple; how modern. But Rockstar hasn't added the ability to do much more simply because it doesn't fit with the story. In a statement to Shacknews Rockstar explains:

"GTA 6 is a game about a couple in a bind, lovers on the run. While we have taken a lot forward from previous GTA titles, everything we have implemented in [GTA 6] has been done to support the spirit of the story we wanted to tell, and the gameplay systems we wanted to expand upon—things like the wanted system, the radio, robberies and car theft. Many aspects of previous titles are not present in GTA 6, but the elements we have we believe are all necessary and complementary to the feeling and motivations we wanted to emphasise as you play through Jason and Lucia's story."

Honestly, it makes sense. Given the fact that this story clearly revolves around the two of them you'd probably have a considerably worse time towards the end if there was an option to break the couple up. It's bad enough running into your ex in public, but imagine having to do a bank heist with them? Yeah, no thanks.

I'm sure once (or whenever) GTA 6 online comes out players will be able to do whatever they please. But for now you'll have to stay within the confine of GTA 6's storylines, which means being in a loving relationship, how sad.

After considerable speculation and a plethora of reports, it was finally confirmed this week that Robert Pattinson would take on the mantle of James Bond. I personally didn’t have my money on the Batman actor trading in his cape for a suit, but I'm not mad at it! Now, additional details are starting to reach the surface, as it's been alleged that Pattinson was pulled into an audition after executives were struggling to make a decision. With that, he was allegedly paid a large sum of money to test for the role, and it seems a lot more of that green could come his way.

According to a report from The Mirror, the Dune actor received $1 million just to audition for 007. To say that's a considerable amount of money would be an understatement. However, Amazon MGM Studios has neither confirmed nor denied that total. As surreal as that sum might seem, there's more to this.

Pattinson -- who has since been congratulated by the British Royal Family and more -- the Royal Family welcomed him as the next Bond. Apparently, the Drama star has signed a three-year deal to play Commander Bond and could allegedly make somewhere between £58 million ($76 million) and £75 million ($98 million). Again, none of this is confirmed, but such a paycheck would make sense, given the deal and the sheer size of this storied IP.

Meanwhile, fans have mixed reactions to the casting news, with some already on board with seeing Pattinson’s take on 007 and others feeling like there were other prime options. A number of notable stars were in the mix before Pattinson was cast, with Jack Lowden notably emerging as a reported favorite. Some may wonder how Pattinson was decided upon and, per an insider, the process wasn't cut and dry.

Per a source for The Mirror, Amazon founder Jeff Bezos' wife, Lauren Sanchez, was a major proponent of Robert Pattinson being cast in the role. Sanchez has allegedly long been a fan of the Primetime star and supposedly helped push him to the forefront when it came to Bond casting. The insider said:

Robert wasn’t the name everyone was talking about. There were other actors who seemed much further down the road. Then, suddenly, he was the man everybody wanted. Lauren’s push for him was hardly a secret in certain circles. Jeff might be the man with the billions, but Lauren has his ear.

Details on Bond 26 are being kept under wraps, including the title and premise. At this point, it also feels unlikely that it'll be released in 2027. However, we do know that Denis Villeneuve will be directing the movie, meaning this will be a Dune reunion for him and Pattinson. There is a lot of speculation surrounding who will join Pattinson, as names are being thrown out for the next Bond villain. And, of course, many are wondering who will be the next Bond girl with rumors placing Margaret Qualley in the lead as a strong candidate.

Regardless of what actually unfolds within the next 007 movie, this new report suggests that Robert Pattinson will be well compensated for the role. What's more is that this reported deal comes near the end of a year that saw him headline multiple high-profile movies. And, of course, can be seen in the upcoming Dune: Part Three, as well as 2028's The Batman: Part II. Needless to say, the man is booked and busy.

Pattinson's clearly come a long way, from playing a sparkling vampire in Twilight to playing a doomed young wizard in Harry Potter. Now, he can add being the ninth James Bond to his resume (and his bank account may be fuller for it).

#3737. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 is the US' best-selling physical game so far this year

The very popular and critically-acclaimed The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has set another record. After selling 5.2m copies in four days and becoming the Switch 2's fastest-selling game, Ocarina of Time has now been revealed to also be a major seller at retail.

The remake has sold more than 1m physical copies in the US alone in its launch week (ending 7th November). That's according to Circana analyst Mat Piscatella, who revealed on Bluesky that the record also makes it the first title to surpass 1m physical sales since 2023's Tears of the Kingdom. That is, no other game - from any publisher - has managed to sell over 1m copies in the US within its first week in three years.

While Nintendo games tend to perform better at retail than those from Sony, Xbox or third-party publishers, physical sales in general have been declining in the US. In July, Piscatella revealed that just seven PlayStation games have sold more than 100,000 physical copies up to that point in 2026, and that was after all the backlash to Sony's decision to end physical disc manufacturing by January 2028.

Ocarina of Time's lead of this particular segment likely won't continue, however. That's because, as Piscatella pointed out in a follow-up post, Circana's tracking considers disc-less, code-in-box versions to be physical editions. This means Grand Theft Auto 6 will likely overtake the remake in short order, just as it's expected to break records elsewhere.

In Eurogamer's glowing review of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, Christian Donlan argued that Nintendo has done just enough to modernise a timeless classic while maintaining what made the original so special for many players.

Ubisoft has been slowly rolling out mass layoffs since its big restructure earlier this year, and its latest will directly affect the studios responsible for games like Assassin's Creed and Far Cry. Well over 100 developers will lose their jobs at Ubisoft Montréal and Ubisoft Québec.

"Ubisoft is reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations," the company says in a statement provided to IGN and other outlets. "As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs."

The company's statement does not specify which projects are affected by the layoffs, though IGN reports that the layoffs primarily affect employees who'd been working on canceled or reworked games. (Both GamesIndustry.biz and VGC offer near-identical background reporting on the nature of the layoffs.)

The Montréal studio has been around since 1997, and is one of the publisher's flagship development houses, leading development on the Splinter Cell, Prince of Persia, Far Cry, and Assassin's Creed franchises over the years. It's now leading development on Assassin's Creed Hexe. Ubisoft Québec has similarly led many Assassin's Creed titles, including Odyssey and Shadows.

Both offices are now part of Vantage Studios, a Tencent-backed subsidiary focused on developing games in the Assassin's Creed, Far Cry, and Rainbow Six series. Some of Ubisoft's Montréal operation is now also part of Massive Entertainment, which primarily handles Tom Clancy-branded titles, including The Division, Ghost Recon, and Splinter Cell.

"We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognize the impact this may have on our colleagues," Ubisoft's statement concludes. "We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources."

Awesome Games Done Quick, one of the biggest speedrunning events of the year, was officially announced yesterday for January 3 to 10, 2027. As ever, the mix of games is fantastic, with huge, AAA titles interwoven with all-time classics and teeny indie favorites. Where else can you watch the N64’sÂ PokÃ©mon Snap followed up by 2026 platformerÂ Denshattack!, or Tomb Raider: Underworld finished in under half an hour before sitting down twoÂ Bayonetta 3 completed in 120 minutes. And let’s not forget the 25 minutes the Atari 2600’sÂ E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial is expected to last.

Wednesday afternoon has an especially good line-up, with PokÃ©mon Violet, 2026’s remake ofÂ Star Fox, and thenÂ Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots all in a row. But it’s Thursday evening that really stands out. Starting at just after 5 p.m. ET, you’ve got the extraordinaryÂ Dustforce DX, thenÂ Halo: Reach, and freshly added to the schedule comesÂ Queen’s Domain followed at around 9.18 p.m. by Ocarina of Time. #3734. Sci-fi RPG Exodus continues evoking Mass Effect by revealing female lead and nicknaming her FemJun

Sci-fi role-playing game Exodus continues to play into the Mass Effect comparisons by revealing the female version of its main character Jun, and with studio Archetype referring to her in marketing material as FemJun.

If that moniker sounds familiar it's because it is: the female Commander Shepard character in the Mass Effect series was nicknamed FemShep. FemShep became an iconic part of BioWare's iconic series, eventually proving that female leads could front games just as successfully as male leads could, and be every bit as popular.

Is the nickname FemJun too blatant? Possibly. But there's well publicised BioWare pedigree at Archetype Entertainment, in the studio's co-founders and in the people leading the project. Key Mass Effect writer Drew Karpyshyn is in charge of writing Exodus, for example, and the similarities to Mass Effect are something the Exodus team has not been shy about in the past. In the wake of Mass Effect 5 being cancelled and BioWare being closed, they become even more alluring.

There are, however, big and important differences between Exodus and Mass Effect, key among them, time dilation. In Exodus, there are special Exodus missions whereby you leave your home planet and fly far away, and in doing so experience time differently to the people back home. Many years will pass for them while only days will pass for you, which provides the game with a way to show you long-term consequences of your actions when you return.

Archetype hasn't shown the female version of Jun before, despite having released many videos of Exodus, perhaps to build anticipation for her reveal. It's a press beat that's also provided Archetype - a studio owned by Dungeons & Dragons company Wizards of the Coast - with an occasion to reveal the two actors playing Jun in the game.

Female Jun is portrayed by Carina Conti, who played the lead in the recent Mafia game, The Old Country - Isabella Torrisi. She's appeared in HBO's Winning Time and Hulu/Freeform's Good Trouble as well. Male Jun, meanwhile, is portrayed by Stephen Oyoung, who played Mister Negative in Insomniac's Marvel's Spider-Man 1 and 2 games, and Red Hood in Gotham Knights. He also appeared in Mission: Impossible - The Final Reckoning, The Wrecking Crew, and Twisters. The game also famously stars Matthew McConaughey.

Archetype announced a Dark Horse hardback art book to go on sale alongside the game next year as well. This arrives a week after the game; Exodus arrives 7th April 2027 on PC, PS5 and Xbox Series S/X, and the art book on 13th April.

Matt played Exodus at Gamescom relatively recently and came away impressed, referring to it as "the best kind of surprise". "I wasn't expecting quite such a bombastic 45 minutes when I first picked up a controller and settled into Exodus, admittedly, but the more I played, the more it made sense," he wrote. "I might not be much of a Mass Effect fan (damn you M35 Mako once more), but Exodus is now firmly on my radar ahead of its arrival next year."

#3732. Xbox Hardware Sales Finally Saw A Major Surge Ahead Of GTA In The U.S.

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4Gears Of War: E-DayStar WarsXbox Series X/S

Xbox dollar sales were up a whopping 42 percent in October year-over-year, a sort of dramatic rise that I feel like I haven’t seen in a while from Xbox.

This is according to Circana’s monthly report, published today. In hardware, spending was up 2 percent year-over-year. Both PlayStation and Xbox sales grew year-over-year, with PlayStation 5 sales up 20 percent from this time last year and Xbox sales up a whopping 42 percent, while Switch sales dropped 11 percent year-over-year.

I was admittedly surprised to see a positive year-over-year growth in Xbox hardware sales, something that’s been rather rare in recent months and even years. Piscatella explained to me that this was a result of some combined factors. The Xbox Series console costs 29 percent more than it did at this time last year, and Circana measures growth in dollar sales. However, in past months, when sales were down, Circana has noted that rising prices were actively discouraging individuals from buying Xboxes. This month, unit sales went up 10 percent.

“Percentages are always tricky because the lower the number is the easier it is to get to a higher percentage change,” Circana’s Mat Piscatella said. “It’s no secret that Xbox Series hardware sales have struggled in recent years. Gears and GTA may have provided at least a temporary reprieve. Of course all bets are off for everyone in November across Ocarina, GTA and even WoW Forever.

“The spending growth was as high as it was primarily because the pricing was so much higher. People did buy more units of Xbox Series this October despite the raised price. Higher pricing generally represses unit volume no matter what product or category one’s looking at (be it grocery, clothes or video game stuff). Just so happens that this October the percentage growth in unit sales of Xbox Series was much smaller than the percentage growth in price which is how pricing drove the spending increase.”

So basically, people are buying Xboxes in preparation for GTA, and also to play Gears. And because Xboxes are so expensive and haven’t sold well recently, that resulted in a pretty significant percentage leap in dollar sales from this time last year. Makes sense!

Unsurprisingly, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 was the best-selling game of October in the 19th consecutive year that a Call of Duty game has dominated its launch month. It was followed by Gears of War: E-Day debuting at No.2 and Star Wars: Galactic Racer debuting at No.3. Other launch games for October included Final Fantasy Resonance (No.6), Kingdom Hearts Collection I-III (No.9), and Nintendo Switch Sports Resort (No.10). None of these new releases cracked the top ten best-selling games of the year so far, which is still led by NBA 2K27 at No.1 and Resident Evil: Requiem at No.2.

Piscatella also shared with me that Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse launched at No.12, and Hellraiser: Revival was at No.15. Dragon’s Dogma II rose from No. 204 in the rankings last month to No.17 this month thanks to the Dark Arisen expansion, and Resident Evil 4 went from No. 64 to No. 31 due to a number of Halloween discounts.

*Data includes digital sales projections. Some publishers, such as Nintendo, do not share digital sales data with Circana and thus estimates are incorporated into their placement.

Overall, consumer content spending on consoles was down 18 percent from last year. Last year, Call of Duty was in November, not October, but October 2025 had both Battlefield 6 and PokÃ©mon Legends: Z-A, which together resulted in more content spending than Call of Duty could pull on its own this year.

The Nintendo Switch 2 is still the best-selling console year-to-date as well as last month, and the PS5 is still in second. The Nintendo Switch 2 limited-edition Zelda-themed Pro Controller was the best-selling accessory of the month. Overall total games spending was down 12 percent year-over-year.

#3731. PlayStation defeats £2 billion UK lawsuit that alleged Sony forced consumers into "excessive and unfair prices"

12.2 million gamers can be wrong, apparently.

Sony has defeated a major £2 billion UK class action lawsuit concerning the price of games on the PlayStation Store (thanks, TheGameBusiness). The judgment came after a 30-day Competition Appeal Tribunal that took place in London, where PlayStation users claimed Sony had removed "all actual and potential competition" in relation to selling digital games on the console.

The case, brought by Alex Neill, who said she represented roughly 12.2 million gamers, accused Sony of applying "excessive and unfair" pricing on games that appeared on the storefront accessible by PS3, PS4 and PS5 consoles - the PlayStation Store. In a judgment published by the London’s Competition Appeal Tribunal today (17th November), the case was rejected. The judgement noted that market definitions used to define Sony's conduct were "unsafe", and that consumers "would be likely to make informed choices when purchasing consoles" and games on the hardware, too.

"Potential PlayStation console purchasers had both access to sufficient information and an incentive to consider that information in order to make informed purchasing decisions at the console level, especially in the case of high-value users who spend significant amounts in the digital gaming aftermarket," read the judgment.

The lawsuit made the argument that, upon purchasing a PS5 or other PlayStation console, you were then trapped within its ecosystem, and forced into paying the prices determined by Sony. The Tribunal disagreed, however, and ruled that Sony competed within a wider 'systems market' alongside Xbox, Nintendo and PC, for example. Furthermore, the Tribunal found no evidence that the existence of other digital storefronts would have actually brought any PlayStation Store pricing down.

Interestingly, the Tribunal used the argument that consumers can also opt and buy physical games instead of using the PlayStation Store - something that is changing as of the start of 2028. That did not seem to have any bearing on today's decision, though. It's also worth noting that this case did not seek to interrogate the ownership status of digital games - something that's been at the heart of the movement rallying against Sony's decision to kill off physical media. Earlier this year, spokespeople from Sony's legal team argued "reasonable consumers" already know they don't actually own their digital games.

The London Tribunal has a fairly long history. Back in 2022, it began as a case that attempted to sue Sony to the tune of £5bn for "ripping people off" on PlayStation Store. Sony argued the case brought against it in this trial was "flawed from start to finish". This isn't the only situation where we're seeing consumers pursue legal action against the platform holder. Last year, PlayStation was sued in the Netherlands over the so-called "Sony tax" that highlighted artificially inflated prices on the Store, and sought to represent more than 20,000 participants that felt short-changed by the company.

The 9-1-1 franchise is heating up amid the 2026 TV schedule. While the fall finales of both the Mothership and 9-1-1: Nashville air this week, there's going to be a lot more on the way in the new year. This includes a much-anticipated I Know What You Did Last Summer reunion between Jennifer Love Hewitt and Ryan Phillippe. I'm excited, but what I didn’t expect was Hewitt’s intense take on working with her former co-star again.

Hewitt and Phillippe starred together in the first IKWYDLS film, which was released back in 1997. While Phillippe’s Barry Cox is eventually murdered in the movie, Hewitt’s Julie James becomes the focal point of the sequels. So it’s been close to 30 years since the original movie, and it's great that Barry and Julie are finally back together in some sense.

Following speculation that Phillippe and Hewitt would be reuniting, Hewitt recently confirmed that he would indeed guest star on 9-1-1, reprising his Nashville role as Detective Rogue Kelly. Surprisingly, this is actually the first time that they’ve seen each other since filming wrapped on IKWYDLS, and Hewitt recalled to People just what the atmosphere felt like before the crossover came together. And her take even makes me a bit anxious:

I was so nervous. I had dry mouth and like a full racy heart. Everybody was like, ‘Are you excited?’ I was like, ‘I feel like I’ve forgotten how to act.’ Yeah, it was amazing. We greeted each other with just a big hug and he was like, ‘This is going to be really fun.’ I said, ‘I think it is.’ And it was just, it was a dream.

I love that even though they’ve worked together before, Hewitt can still have those nerves, and I can’t say I blame her. Reuniting with someone you haven’t seen in years -- even if it's on your own turf -- can be intimidating. It sounds like the mood instantly shifted when Phillippe came to set, in a good way, and it makes me even more excited to see how it all turns out.

Phillippe only joined 9-1-1: Nashville for Season 2, so the fact that the two shows are already jumping at the chance to do a crossover featuring him and Hewitt is pretty great. Plus, seeing Phillippe and Hewitt together again is like a '90s-infused dream, and it sounds like they had the time of their lives. Hewitt admitted just how much fun they’ve had from seeing the Internet reacting to the news. She also shared how great it’s been to welcome Phillippe to the 9-1-1 Universe, especially after she reunited with Freddie Prinze Jr. for 2025’s I Know What You Did Last Summer:

He and I have had the best time with people’s reaction. We’ve been DMing going, ‘Did you see it?’ I think we broke the internet. We’ve been having the best time. It was so great because I got to go back and do the movie with Freddie [Prinze Jr.] and sort of have that, and do [our characters] Julie James and Ray again. But this was very different because it was like, [Ryan’s] new in that universe. I’ve been in this universe for a while. It’s such a safe, lovely place to be with the best people. And he and I have not seen each other since I was 18 years old.

As for right now, details surrounding the next 9-1-1 and 9-1-1: Nashville crossover have not been revealed, and I'm eager to see what brings Rogue to Los Angeles. After trying to track down a serial killer in Nashville who is using biblical plagues, hopefully this trip out West will be a bit lighter for him. Of course, if anyone can help him, it’s Hewitt’s Maddie Buckley-Han, who is arguably the best 9-1-1 dispatcher in LA.

Hopefully, crossover information is announced soon, but considering the amount of content Jennifer Love Hewitt has been sharing on her Instagram, she is probably going to keep fans fed for the time being.

For now, viewers can tune in for the fall finales of 9-1-1 and 9-1-1: Nashville, which air this Thursday, November 19, at 8 p.m. ET on ABC, streaming the next day with a Hulu subscription. Both shows will then return from their midseason breaks on Thursday, January 7.

#3729. The Game Awards just confirmed who plays GTA 6's Lucia

Manni L. Perez has been confirmed as the actress behind Grand Theft Auto 6's Lucia Caminos, just days before the game launches.

As spotted by IGN, the confirmation came during The Game Awards' nominations livestream today, where Perez was nominated for Best Performance for her role as co-lead Lucia.

Perez had been widely rumoured to play Lucia for months, and fans have regularly filled her social media livestreams with questions about GTA 6, which she has been oh-so-carefully sidestepping.

Lucia is one half of GTA 6's lead pair alongside Jason Duval, making it the first Grand Theft Auto game with a playable couple.

Jason's actor wasn't among the nominees, so who plays him is still a mystery.

Perez has previously had guest roles in a string of US TV dramas, including Law & Order: Special Victims Unit, Chicago P.D., The Blacklist, and Blindspot, and has also done voice work for GTA Online.

Funnily enough, Lucia isn't her first Lucia - she also played Lucia Santiago in a 2023 episode of CBS's East New York.

GTA 6 arrives 19th November on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It is now available to pre-load for anyone who pre-ordered the digital version, and those with the code-in-box physical version.

It's long been revealed that GTA 6 will have a regional release, meaning that some lucky, soon-to-be players will be able to access the game much earlier than others. Rockstar's regional release schedule sees the game launching at midnight on 19th November regardless of what region you're in, and if you wish to join those playing almost a day early, there's the good ol' Xbox New Zealand trick for eager players to try.

#3728. Rockstar Kept One Of GTA 6’s Biggest Early Spoilers Under Wraps For Years

Inevitably, my day job of keeping up with the biggest video game release of the past decade is going to put me in spoiler territory, but Iâm pretty pleased that I was able to avoid one of Grand Theft Auto 6âs big secrets until I started playing the game when it went live this morning. Spoilers ahead if you havenât been able to start the game yet, but this is something you learn in the opening hour, so weâre not talking endgame reveals here. This fact has now made it nearly impossible for me to even consider a hyperviolent run, when I already felt like these games donât really do the legwork needed to make that playstyle feel âcorrectâ in the grand scheme of the satirical soap-opera stories theyâre telling.

Jason and Lucia, the criminal couple at the center of GTA 6, have a son. His name is TomÃ¡s and heâs just a baby at the beginning of the game. Lucia, desperate for cash, left him at a dinerâshe planned to come right back!â during the stickup that landed her in prison, which is where we find her when the game proper begins. GTA6 goes to some lengths to obfuscate TomÃ¡sâ existence in these opening segments with strategic camera angles that ensure you never see him in his carrier, and frantic dialogue between Lucia and a server that gets interrupted just before either of them can reveal that the little man is there. So when you inevitably get caught after your attempted heist, youâre not sure why Lucia is begging the cops to let her go back to the restaurant.

Then, itâs revealed, a group of staff and patrons are all gathered around the crying baby whose mama left him and is now in the back of a cop car. This whole mess is explained in a flashback as Lucia tells a social worker about why she was arrested, and why sheâd be a good candidate for a monitored release program as the prison seeks to open up a bed or two to account for an overflow of incoming inmates. Though Lucia is told that getting out with an ankle monitor on her leg is a separate matter from her being able to see her son again, she swears that this arrest has been a wake-up call for her and Jason, and that theyâre ready to live an honest life.

Well, this is Grand Theft Auto, so an âhonest lifeâ is all relative, I suppose. But the knowledge that Jason and Lucia could be responsible for someone elseâs livelihood does recontextualize things. Like most folks, Iâm still very early in the game, but GTA 6 has a morality system that tracks how you carry out your criminal activities. Thus far in my game, Lucia is still incarcerated and Iâm playing as Jason, doing odd jobs until she gets out, but in these early missions, Iâve been making a point to do things as quickly and quietly as I can.Â

At first, this decision wasnât even grounded in any narrative or roleplaying; itâs how I tend to play action games that have a stealth option. Treating thugs and cops like clockwork puzzles to be solved comes more naturally to me than going in guns blazing. Despite mayhem and carnage being one of the most famous features of Grand Theft Auto, Iâve never really felt that the framework of these games supports you opening fire on a group of civilians. It feels like a glitch in the Matrix, though I understand that pushing those boundaries and having a virtual excuse to behave badly is part of the cathartic appeal for some folks.Personally, however, I donât usually feel the compulsion to wreak havoc on passersby, so I donât spend time in games like Grand Theft Auto or Cyberpunk ruining strangersâ days.

But now, knowing that reuniting a family is a major piece of this puzzle, that disconnect feels more prominent than ever. In some ways, I can see the argument that Jason and Lucia could be willing to go to great lengths to reunite with their son and give him a comfortable life; Iâm just not sure I see explosions and constant carnage on the path to that future now. Hey, maybe something will happen later in the game that will change my mind, but for now, Iâm about to try and keep these twoâs hands (relatively) clean.

Musical virtuoso and the undisputed GOAT of song parodies 'Weird Al' Yankovic has confirmed his inclusion in GTA 6 as a radio host.

Earlier this week, Weird Al posted saying, "Apologies in advance to any friends or loved ones who may want to have some kind of human interaction with me in the upcoming week. I'll be playing a video game." While that seemed very much in line with the litany of people – famous or otherwise – who are going to dedicate their time to GTA 6 over the next week or so, as people got access to the game , they realized it's weirder than they thought. Vice City FM – home of '80s bangers like Prefab Sprout's Cars and Girls and The The's This Is the Day – is hosted by Mr Yankovic himself.

In a post on BlueSky, Weird Al posts an image saying, "now that my NDA has expired… Hey, everybody, I'm in GTA 6." He adds, "I'm the host of GTA 6's 'non-stop '80s' radio channel Vice City FM," which most people had already gathered, marking his second-ever video game appearance after being the announcer for The Grim Adventures of Billy and Mandy – a Power Stone clone for the PS2 and Wii.

I’m the host of GTA 6’s “non-stop ‘80s” radio channel Vice City FM. I also wrote some in-game commercials, and I’m the voice of the Burger Shot ads as well! As a long-time fan of the Grand Theft Auto franchise, I couldn’t be more excited about this. Okay, gotta get back to playing the game!

But as it turns out, his contributions are more than just a radio host. Weird Al confirms "I also wrote some in-game commercials, and I'm the voice of the Burger Shot ads as well!" The game's credits also list him as a contributor of original music for the game – although unfortunately none of his songs are featured on the in-game radio stations. He adds, "As a long-time fan of the Grand Theft Auto franchise, I couldn't be more excited about this. Okay, gotta get back to playing the game!"

Weird Al is joined by the likes of pop icons Robyn, Gloria Estefan, and PinkPantheress, as well as Fleetwood Mac's Lindsey Buckingham, Yacht Rock king Michael McDonald and Oscar, Tony, Emmy, and Golden Globe winning actor Jeremy Irons as DJ Dicky.

EXCLUSIVE: This is Lenovo's upcoming Legion Go Beam, a new gaming handheld that appears to be a more affordable alternative to the premium Legion Go 2: https://t.co/T5Nrh5VAig pic.twitter.com/JdLI9QrzsKNovember 18, 2026

With the pricing of memory right now, it's hard to get too excited for gaming handhelds, but Lenovo's reportedly more budget-friendly Legion Go Beam does intrigue me. And, with a recent leak, I'm now looking forward to hearing about the full details in the new year.

This leak comes courtesy of Windows Latest, which managed to get its hands on three images, plus the name, and a suggestion that it will be less expensive than the Legion Go 2. Admittedly, the Legion Go 2 and its OLED screen are climbing up to $2,000 right now, so undercutting that isn't super tough.

The Go Beam has a white shell with lime green accents at the bottom, on the face buttons, around the thumbsticks, and on the start and menu buttons. It's a striking theme, even if I fear grubby fingers will make that white far grimmer in a matter of months.

There is, unfortunately, a lot we don't know about this handheld. We don't know the screen's panel technology; we don't know what size and weight it is; we don't know what processor powers it; we don't have a price point, and we don't yet have a release date.

Windows Latest is guessing it will be cheaper than the Legion Go based on its feature set, which is not a bad call.

You get most of the controls you expect from a modern handheld, with triggers and bumpers, as well as two paddles on the back. There's a single USB Type-C port on the top of the device, and it has a sequence of eight fan holes in the back left.

It is, however, missing the small touchpad under the right thumbstick that comes with the Lenovo Legion Go S (both Windows and SteamOS models). That means navigating the desktop UI could be a little less easy, though at launch it wasn't usable in SteamOS anyways. It also has bigger bezels than the Go 2 and Go S.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

Lenovo has been very fond of AMD with its gaming handhelds thus far, using Ryzen Z2, Z2 Extreme and Ryzen Z2 Go chips, but there is a suggestion the Beam could be kitted with a lower-end Panther Lake chip (perhaps the Intel Arc G3 and its Arc B370 iGPU). I haven't spent much time with the G3, but I have been very impressed with the G3 Extreme, from both a performance and battery life perspective.

With Lenovo attending CES at the start of 2027, Windows Latest reckons that is when we will see more about this handheld. But it does note that Lenovo doesn't mention gaming for the January show, so it could be holding out for later in 2027, perhaps Computex in June.

Either way, if Lenovo is putting out cheaper handhelds, that's certainly not bad news for us PC gamers, even if we're still going to be paying an arm and a leg for the memory and storage inside it.

#3725. Firaxis reportedly cuts a third of its staff as studio head departs and new XCOM struggles

Civilization and XCOM developer Firaxis Games has laid off around 60 people.

The cuts, which took place today, account for about a third of the studio’s staff, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter. Studio head Heather Hazen is also leaving.

Its sources say Firaxis' unannounced XCOM game has faced development struggles and missed "a significant milestone over the summer". The project will continue, but "may face a shakeup as a result of the cuts".

A spokesperson for 2K, the Take-Two label that runs Firaxis, confirmed Hazen's departure to Bloomberg, and said the studio is "restructuring and recentering around the studio's core strength - designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years".

"As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis," the spokesperson continued. "These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis."

The layoffs come two days before the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, which is developed and published by Rockstar, a separate label at Take-Two.

In September, around 18 months after Civ 7's widely criticised launch - and as the legendary 4X series celebrates its 35th anniversary - Firaxis unveiled a host of new updates coming to the game as it continued to improve it. These included an atomic age update, dragging Civ 7 into the present and beyond, as well as its first paid expansion, Earthrise, both arriving next year.

Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick admitted earlier this year that the studio "got it wrong with Civ 7".

"The game is a really good game. And it's certainly a profitable enterprise for us. But this is one where I think what we tried to do was a bridge too far, from the consumer's perspective," he told Game File in May.

It’s not the first round of cuts at the studio - 2K confirmed an unspecified number of layoffs at Firaxis in September 2025, and around 30 jobs went in 2023.

#3724. The Game Awards 2026 nominees announced, and GTA 6 leads with eight nods before it's even out

The Game Awards 2026 nominees have been revealed, and Grand Theft Auto 6 leads the pack with eight nominations, two days before it even launches.

Rockstar's crime epic is up for Game of the Year, Best Game Direction, Best Narrative, Best Art Direction, Best Score and Music, Best Audio Design, and Best Action/Adventure Game. Its eighth nomination is Manni L. Perez's Best Performance nod for her role as Lucia, which is how we found out who plays her in the first place.

THE GAME AWARDS: 2026 Nominee Reveal! (Game of the Year) THE GAME AWARDS: 2026 Nominee Reveal!Watch on YouTube

For Game of the Year, GTA 6 is up against 007 First Light, Control Resonant, Phantom Blade Zero, Resident Evil Requiem, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Nintendo is the most-nominated publisher, with 12 nominations across its games, followed by Capcom with 11, and Annapurna Interactive and PlayStation with nine each.

The nominees were picked by a jury of more than 160 media and creator outlets, who may get advance or pre-release access to games - which explains how GTA 6 made the cut before launch. The winners will be revealed on Thursday, 10th December, at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. Fans can vote on The Game Awards' website until 6pm PT on 9th December.

This year's show will stream for free on more than 40 platforms, including YouTube, Twitch, Prime Video, and Steam. Last year's show drew an estimated 171 million livestreams, up 11 percent on 2024's 154 million.
